chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
The waiting period (iddah) is from the water.

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period (iddah) a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarrying.
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: Literally 'water', here referring to menstrual blood (hayd) as the marker for the start of the iddah.

ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a woman divorced before consummation?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the iddah for a woman divorced before consummation is determined by her first menstrual cycle, reflecting the juristic consensus that 'waiting' implies a period of potential pregnancy. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on biological markers over the mere pronouncement of talaq, distinguishing this ruling from the general three-month iddah for non-menstruating women.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘
The waiting period is from the water’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ibn Muskan from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘ Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ’
Waiting period is because of water (seed, semen)/”
